summary: MARS 2030 – THE FIRST COLONY is an interactive 3D Mars exploration and colony survival simulator developed to demonstrate the challenges of establishing human life beyond Earth. We developed this project to make learning about Mars exploration more engaging and help users understand the difficulties astronauts may face while building a sustainable settlement. Players explore the Martian surface, collect resources, construct colony infrastructure, and manage essential survival needs such as oxygen, water, food, and electricity. The simulator also introduces environmental challenges such as dust storms, which can affect visibility and solar power generation. By combining exploration, construction, and resource management, the project addresses the challenge through an interactive learning experience. It is important because it promotes awareness of space exploration, sustainable resource utilization, engineering solutions, and the technologies needed for future human missions to Mars.
details:
MARS 2030 — THE FIRST COLONY is an interactive 3D Mars exploration, colony construction, and human survival simulator built with Three.js and WebGL. Set in the year 2030, players command the first human expedition to Jezero Crater basin, tasked with establishing a self-sustaining human outpost and keeping the commander alive under real Martian environmental hazards.

Key Features & How It Works:

• Realistic 3D Exploration & Kinematics: Features an articulated NASA spacesuit character with two-bone leg and arm kinematics, running locomotion, and a smooth camera system supporting seamless Third-Person and First-Person Commander perspectives (via the 'V' key).

• Physical Walkthrough Pressurized Habitat: Players construct full-scale human habitat domes (17.6m diameter) and physically enter through animated hydraulic sliding blast doors without wall teleportation into an interior equipped with ECLSS life support, crew bunks, water recycling, and mission command consoles.

• Colony Construction Grid: A real-time 3D printing system supporting 10 functional modules including MOXIE solid-oxide oxygen reactors, solar arrays, lithium battery storage matrices, aeroponic greenhouses, and water extraction drills.

• Dynamic Regional Dust Storms: A 3-stage atmospheric event simulating optical depth attenuation (>85% solar drop), suit dust abrasion, and thermal drops, requiring players to seek shelter and balance energy reserves.

• Real-Time Life Support (ECLSS): Metabolic and thermodynamic tracking of oxygen mass balance, water reclamation, internal suit temperature, heart rate, and atmospheric CO₂ scrubbing.

Tools & Technologies Used:

• 3D & Graphics: Three.js (r170), WebGL, Custom PBR shaders, Procedural Texturing

• Core Stack: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas, Modern CSS3 Glassmorphism

• Build & CI/CD: Vite, Node.js, Git, GitHub Actions automated deployment

• Audio: Web Audio API (synthesized spatial acoustics, airlock hydraulics, howling winds)

• Scientific Reference: NASA Open Data from Perseverance & Curiosity missions at Jezero Crater.

Impact & Innovation:

The simulator transforms complex NASA aerospace engineering and life-support trade-offs into an intuitive, visually captivating educational experience that teaches students and space enthusiasts the real science of interplanetary colonization.
